request.prompt:
A rider who uses a wheelchair travels this weekend from 59 St-Columbus Circle to 34 St-Hudson Yards using only the services and free transfers shown on this map. Walking between stations joined on the map counts as a transfer, and the trip ends when a train arrives at 34 St-Hudson Yards itself. They can only enter, leave or change trains at stations marked with the accessibility symbol. They want the fewest transfers and, among those trips, the fewest station stops. Which services do they ride, in order? If more than one service runs between the same two stations on a leg, any of them is accepted. Answer as a JSON list of route letters or numbers, for example ["A", "7"].

Answer the question using the image. Think it through, then give the answer as a JSON list of names exactly as written on the map, in order, e.g. ["A", "7"].
End your reply with a final line of the form:
FINAL ANSWER: <answer>

content:
The fewest-transfer trip is 1, then S, then 7: two transfers.

1. From 59 St-Columbus Circle, take the 1 (accessible, no transfer) to Times Sq-42 St.
2. At Times Sq-42 St, transfer to the S shuttle (free walking transfer) to Grand Central-42 St.
3. At Grand Central-42 St, transfer to the 7 toward 34 St-Hudson Yards.

Reaching the 7 at Times Sq isn't possible because 7 trains run through that station without stopping. Grand Central is the only accessible stop on the 7 line where it can be boarded, and no line serves it directly from 59 St-Columbus Circle, so two transfers is the minimum.

FINAL ANSWER: ["1", "S", "7"]

I'm working out a route from 59 St-Columbus Circle to 34 St-Hudson Yards, which only the 7 train serves. Since Times Sq-42 St is closed to 7 trains, I'm checking whether to board from Grand Central or 5 Av and trace the 7 line's path westward from the Hudson Yards end.

I'm weighing whether the 7 train's route west of Times Sq actually matters here, since the Port Authority stop on the ACE line sits near the same spot and offers a free transfer.

I'm checking whether the Port Authority stop works as a way to reach the 7, since 7 trains skip Port Authority and I need a station where the 7 actually stops. The accessible stations I'm listing so far are 42 St-Port Authority and Times Sq-42 St.

I'm weighing a route through the S shuttle at Times Sq, since the 7 skips that stop while it's closed, and checking whether a train from 59 St-Columbus Circle can get me there more simply.

I'm checking whether the 7 train can be boarded from Times Sq at all, given the closure, or whether the S shuttle to Grand Central is needed to reach it. I'm also comparing a free transfer at Times Sq with a one-seat option on the 1.

I'm weighing two routes that each take two transfers. One starts with the 1 to Times Sq, then the S shuttle to Grand Central to pick up the 7. The other starts with the A or C to 42 St-Port Authority and continues from there.

I'm weighing S shuttle transfers at Times Sq against a Grand Central option, since 1 can't reach Grand Central and 7 doesn't stop at Times Sq while it's closed. Both routes come out to two transfers, so I'm checking whether one of them is simpler.

I'm considering a one-transfer option by boarding the 7 at Grand Central, but I can't see a way to get from 59 St-Columbus Circle to Grand Central with a single ride, so the two-transfer route through the 1 and S stays the simplest.

I'm settling on 1 to Times Sq, the S shuttle to Grand Central, then the 7, since the 1 can't reach Grand Central and the 7 skips Times Sq while it's closed. Both A and 1 start with about two stops before the first transfer, so the choice between them is close to even.
